turns.prompt_text: I have a roku for the tv, I plug it into the hdmi, but it seems to be trying to connect every 3 seconds but not working
turns.response_html:
When a Roku continuously drops and tries to reconnect every few seconds, it is usually caught in a handshake loop or suffering from micro-power cuts.

Here is a quick triage workflow to isolate and fix the issue, ordered from the most likely culprits to the least.

1. The Power Source (Most Common)

If the Roku is plugged into the TV's USB port for power, the TV likely isn't supplying enough consistent amperage. When the Roku tries to boot or connect to video/Wi-Fi, its power draw spikes, causing it to brown out, crash, and restart every few seconds.

  • The Fix: Unplug the USB cable from the TV and plug it directly into a dedicated wall outlet adapter (like a cell phone charging brick).

2. HDMI Handshake Loop

HDMI uses a copy-protection protocol called HDCP. If the TV and the Roku fail to shake hands, the TV will drop the signal, wait three seconds, and try to establish a handshake again.

  • The Fix: Perform a hard hardware reset to clear the HDMI cache:
    1. Unplug the Roku from both the HDMI port and its power source.
    2. Unplug the TV from the wall outlet.
    3. Wait 60 full seconds (this completely drains the capacitors in both devices).
    4. Plug the TV back in and turn it on.
    5. Plug the Roku back into power first, then plug it back into the HDMI port.

3. Physical Port or Cord Failure

Sometimes the issue is physical degradation of the pins inside the connection or a degraded cable.

  • Try a different HDMI port: Switch from HDMI 1 to HDMI 2 or 3.
  • Remove any extensions: If you are using an HDMI extension cable or an HDMI switcher/splitter, bypass it completely and plug the Roku directly into the TV.
  • Check for sag: If it's a Roku streaming stick, the weight of the stick can sometimes tweak the HDMI port downward, breaking pin contact. Try using a short HDMI extension cable to take the strain off the port.

4. Resolution Mismatch

If the Roku is outputting a display setting (like 4K HDR) that the specific HDMI port doesn't support, the TV will repeatedly reject the input.

  • The Fix: If you have another television in the house, plug the Roku into that one. If it works there, go into the Roku settings under Settings > Display Type and change it from "Auto" to a fixed resolution like 1080p. Then bring it back to the original TV.

Which power setup are you currently using for the Roku, and does the screen go completely black when it drops, or does it show a specific "No Signal" logo?

Ah, you have a Roku Streaming Stick Plus (Model 3830X).

Looking at the photo, the root cause of your 3-second connection loop is immediately clear: You are using a generic USB power cable.

The Roku Streaming Stick Plus requires a very specific proprietary cable called the Roku Advanced Wireless Receiver. That original cable has a large, distinct plastic bulge right in the middle of the cord. That bulge isn't just decoration—it houses the actual Wi-Fi and remote control antenna hardware for the device.

Why it's failing:

Because the Wi-Fi receiver is missing from this generic cable, the Roku stick boots up, realizes it has absolutely no network hardware attached to it, fails its initial hardware check, and instantly crashes or reboots to try again. This creates that continuous 3-second connection loop you are experiencing.

How to fix it:

  1. Find the original cable: Look around for the thick USB power cable that came in the original Roku box. It will have a prominent, long plastic rectangle integrated into the wire.
  2. Get a replacement: If the original cable is lost or damaged, a standard micro-USB cable will not work for this specific model. You will need to search for a "Roku Advanced Wireless Receiver cable" online to get the stick functioning again.

This screen is your TV's built-in automatic device detection wizard (typical of Samsung TVs). It pops up whenever it senses a brand-new device handshake on the HDMI port. Because your Roku is dropping out and reconnecting every few seconds, it keeps triggering the TV to throw this menu up over and over again.

Here is what you should do right now:

  • Select "Later": Click "Later" to dismiss this prompt. Trying to run through the "Setup" right now won't fix anything because the TV can't properly communicate with a device that isn't maintaining a stable connection.
  • Focus on the stable connection first: Once you get the Roku to stop dropping its signal every 3 seconds (by addressing the power cable or resetting the HDMI port), the TV will automatically recognize it as a "Roku" via HDMI-CEC, and this annoying menu will stop interrupting you.
